names.posthumous: 文明武德大圣大宣孝皇帝

summary: 玄宗第三子；安史乱起，马嵬后北上灵武即位，遥尊玄宗为太上皇；至德二载郭子仪等收复两京；乾元中九节度围安庆绪于邺溃败，史思明再起；宝应元年崩。
summary_en: Third son of Xuanzong; when the An–Shi rebellion broke, after Mawei he went north and took the throne at Lingwu, honoring Xuanzong as Grand Emperor from afar; in the 2nd year of Zhide Guo Ziyi and the others recovered the two capitals; in mid-Qianyuan the nine commissioners besieged An Qingxu at Ye and were routed, and Shi Siming rose again. He died in the 1st year of Baoying.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现艰难中兴之君之态，衣冠从盛唐制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 灵武即位
timeline.summary: 马嵬后北上，即位于灵武，遥尊玄宗为太上皇。
timeline.summary_en: After Mawei he went north, took the throne at Lingwu, and honored Xuanzong as Grand Emperor from afar.

timeline.title: 收复两京
timeline.summary: 郭子仪等借回纥兵复长安、洛阳。
timeline.summary_en: Guo Ziyi and the others, with the Uyghur cavalry, recovered Chang'an and Luoyang.

timeline.title: 九节度相州败
timeline.summary: 围安庆绪于邺，溃败，史思明再起。
timeline.summary_en: They besieged An Qingxu at Ye, were routed, and Shi Siming rose again.

timeline.title: 肃宗崩
timeline.summary: 崩，代宗继；张后等政变未遂。
timeline.summary_en: He died; Daizong succeeded; the coup of Empress Zhang failed.

timeline.title: 肃宗总评
timeline.summary: 艰难即位，两京虽复而河北未靖。
timeline.summary_en: A hard-won throne: the two capitals recovered, but Hebei unquiet.

bio_md:
# 唐肃宗 · 主要事迹

李亨，玄宗第三子。天宝十五载（756）安史之乱中，玄宗幸蜀，太子亨在马嵬与玄宗分道，北上灵武，即皇帝位，改元至德，遥尊玄宗为太上皇——唐室中兴，自灵武始。肃宗以「平叛」为第一要务：至德二载，郭子仪、李光弼等借回纥之兵，收复长安、洛阳两京；然「借兵回纥，遗患无穷」，回纥之骄横，为后日之祸。

乾元元年，肃宗以九节度使围安庆绪于邺城，诸军无统帅，相州一役大溃，史思明乘势再起、杀安庆绪，安史之乱复炽。上元、宝应之际，肃宗病笃，张皇后与李辅国争权，宫闱之乱未已；宝应元年，肃宗崩于长生殿，年五十二。

史评肃宗：「艰难即位，两京虽复而河北未靖。」肃宗以太子之身，于乱中即位，其功在「再造唐室」；然用李辅国、张后，宦官之祸自此始盛；河北藩镇割据之局，亦成于其朝——安史之乱虽平，而唐室之衰，不可复振。

> 参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷010《肃宗纪》、资治通鉴卷218-222。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Heng, third son of Xuanzong. In the 1st year of Zhide (756), in the An–Shi rebellion, Xuanzong fled to Shu; the heir Heng, parting from Xuanzong at Mawei, went north and took the throne at Lingwu, changing the era to Zhide and honoring Xuanzong as Grand Emperor from afar — the restoration of the Tang began at Lingwu. Suzong's first task was the rebellion: in the 2nd year of Zhide Guo Ziyi, Li Guangbi, and the others, with the Uyghur cavalry, recovered the two capitals; but "borrowing the Uyghurs left a lasting plague," and the Uyghurs' arrogance was a disaster to come.

In the 1st year of Qianyuan he sent nine commissioners to besiege An Qingxu at Ye; without a supreme commander, the host was routed at Xiangzhou, and Shi Siming rose again, slew Qingxu, and the rebellion flared anew. In the Shangyuan and Baoying years Suzong lay ill while Empress Zhang and Li Fuguo contended — the palace disorders unended; he died in the Changsheng Hall in the 1st year of Baoying, aged fifty-two.

The histories say: "a hard-won throne: the two capitals recovered, but Hebei unquiet." Suzong, a heir enthroned in the storm, restored the Tang house; but his use of Li Fuguo and Empress Zhang opened the age of eunuch power, and the feudatory division of Hebei was fixed in his reign — the rebellion ended, but the decline of Tang could not be reversed.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 10 ("Benji of Emperor Suzong"), and the *Zizhi Tongjian*, ch. 218–222.
